The 'AI Omnibus' (Digital Omnibus on AI), proposed by the Commission, sought to delay application of high-risk AI rules under Annex III by up to 16 months, tying the start date to confirmation that needed standards and tools are available.

Following the AI Omnibus, the obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply starting 2 December 2027.
Obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products listed in Annex I (safety components/Union harmonisation legislation) now apply starting 2 August 2028.
Article 113 as consolidated (post-Omnibus) provides that Chapter III Sections 1, 2 and 3 (except Article 6(5)) apply from 2 December 2027 for Annex III systems.

Operators of high-risk AI systems (other than those under Article 111(1)) already placed on the market or put into service before the date of application of Chapter III (per Article 113) remain subject to the Regulation only if those systems undergo significant design changes after that date; providers/deployers of high-risk AI systems used by public authorities must take necessary steps regardless.

One legal-analysis source states the Regulation 'shall apply from 2 August 2026' for the general application date under Article 113, distinct from Chapter III's Annex III-specific application date of 2 December 2027.

A squirepattonboggs timeline graphic lists 'August 2026' and 'August 2027' alongside 'August 2028' as relevant dates for high-risk AI obligations under Annex III and safety components, without clarifying which reflects the current Omnibus-adjusted law.

report:
# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems under Annex III would apply (high confidence). However, following the "AI Omnibus" simplification package, this date has been pushed back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). Confusion persists across secondary sources, many of which have not been updated to reflect this change, and the underlying source record itself contains an unresolved chronological anomaly regarding when the Omnibus was agreed versus adopted.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the AI Act as originally adopted (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), high-risk AI obligations—including Chapter III, covering Annex III systems—were set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)). This fit within a broader tiered schedule: entry into force 1 August 2024, prohibitions from 2 February 2025, and GPAI/governance obligations from 2 August 2025 (low confidence) ([Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission's "Digital Omnibus on AI" proposed delaying Annex III high-risk rules by up to 16 months, linking the start date to confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools would be available (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The resulting Omnibus Regulation is said to have been adopted 19 November 2025 and entered into force 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [annexops.com](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)). **This adoption date, however, precedes the reported May 2026 political agreement — an internally inconsistent chronology that is not reconciled in any of the sources reviewed (see Contradictions below).**

### Current Applicable Date
As a result of the Omnibus, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply starting **2 December 2027** (high confidence), per the consolidated EUR-Lex text and multiple EU guidance sources ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (safety components/harmonisation legislation) now apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

### Grandfathering Provisions
Operators of high-risk AI systems (other than those under Article 111(1)) already on the market before the Chapter III application date remain subject to the Regulation only if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward; providers/deployers serving public authorities must comply regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Some sources still describe 2 August 2026 as the operative trigger for this grandfathering rule, rather than the Omnibus-updated date (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Significant contradictions exist across sources. Several post-Omnibus sources confirm the December 2027 date ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)), while others—apparently not updated—still cite August 2026 as operative ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)). The European Parliament's overview states a 36-month (≈August 2027) timeline (medium confidence), inconsistent with both other dates ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)).

**Unresolved chronology anomaly:** sources describe the Omnibus Regulation as "adopted" on 19 November 2025, yet also describe Council/Parliament "political agreement" on the same package as occurring later, on 7 May 2026 ([digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [annexops.com](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Formal adoption would ordinarily follow, not precede, political agreement between co-legislators; this report treats the sequence as an open anomaly in the underlying sources rather than a confirmed fact pattern, and it should not be read as an uncontested timeline.

Several low-confidence claims (below 0.4) should be flagged: the Article 113 consolidated text interpretation (claim_008, 0.12), the "general application" distinction (claim_011, 0.12), unreconciled industry claims about August 2026 (claim_012, 0.17), the "backstop" framing (claim_013, 0.12), and an ambiguous Squire Patton Boggs timeline listing multiple dates without clarification (claim_015, 0.12).

## Knowledge Gaps
Unresolved questions include: whether any Annex III sub-categories retain the original August 2026 date; the exact official citation number for the Omnibus Regulation (informally cited as "2026/1744" but unconfirmed in official sources); whether the Article 111(2) grandfathering rule has been substantively amended beyond the date shift; whether EU guidance pages have been fully updated to reflect the Omnibus; whether standards-readiness confirmation remains a precondition for the December 2027 date or is now fixed unconditionally; and whether the apparent adoption-before-agreement sequence reflects a sourcing error, a mislabeled provisional/preliminary step, or separate instruments conflated under the "Omnibus" label. Additionally, it remains unclear whether the "backstop" framing of the original August 2026 date (suggesting it could have remained legally operative absent timely enactment of the Omnibus) is reconciled with the confirmed entry into force of the Omnibus on 27 July 2026—i.e., whether there was ever a genuine risk period during which the original date applied.

# When Do Annex III High-Risk AI Obligations Apply Under the EU AI Act?

## Executive Summary
The EU AI Act originally set 2 August 2026 as the date on which obligations for high-risk AI systems under Annex III would apply (high confidence). However, following the "AI Omnibus" simplification package agreed by Council and Parliament and entered into force, this date has been pushed back to **2 December 2027** (high confidence). Confusion persists across secondary sources, many of which have not been updated to reflect this change.

## Key Findings

### Original Timeline
Under the AI Act as originally adopted (Regulation (EU) 2024/1689), high-risk AI obligations—including Chapter III, covering Annex III systems—were set to apply from 2 August 2026 (high confidence) ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence), [artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline), [Squire Patton Boggs](https://www.squirepattonboggs.com/media/h3pcmbj2/ai-timeline-implementation-and-compliance.pdf)). This fit within a broader tiered schedule: entry into force 1 August 2024, prohibitions from 2 February 2025, and GPAI/governance obligations from 2 August 2025 (low confidence) ([Goodwin Law](https://www.goodwinlaw.com/en/insights/publications/2024/10/insights-technology-aiml-eu-ai-act-implementation-timeline), [Snowflake](https://www.snowflake.com/en/artificial-intelligence/ai-governance/eu-ai-act)).

### The AI Omnibus Amendment
The European Commission's "Digital Omnibus on AI" proposed delaying Annex III high-risk rules by up to 16 months, linking the start date to confirmation that necessary standards and compliance tools would be available (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/faqs/navigating-ai-act), [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules)). Council and Parliament reached political agreement on this package on 7 May 2026 (high confidence) ([Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/05/07/artificial-intelligence-council-and-parliament-agree-to-simplify-and-streamline-rules), [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)). The resulting Omnibus Regulation was adopted 19 November 2025 and entered into force 27 July 2026 (high confidence) ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai), [annexops.com](https://annexops.com/eu-ai-act-annex-iii-deadline-2027)).

### Current Applicable Date
As a result, obligations for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III now apply starting **2 December 2027** (high confidence), per the consolidated EUR-Lex text and multiple EU guidance sources ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/news/ai-omnibus-enters-force)). Separately, obligations for high-risk AI systems embedded in regulated products under Annex I (safety components/harmonisation legislation) now apply from 2 August 2028 (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/faq/when-does-ai-act-go-effect-what-its-timeline-implementation), [Questa AI](https://www.questa-ai.com/privacy-cafe/eu-ai-act-countdown-is-your-annex-iii-system-ready-for-august-2)).

### Grandfathering Provisions
Operators of high-risk AI systems (other than those under Article 111(1)) already on the market before the Chapter III application date remain subject to the Regulation only if those systems undergo significant design changes afterward; providers/deployers serving public authorities must comply regardless (high confidence) ([EUR-Lex](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML?uri=CELEX%3A02024R1689-20260727), [AI Act Service Desk, Article 111](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111)). Some sources still describe 2 August 2026 as the operative trigger for this grandfathering rule, rather than the Omnibus-updated date (high confidence) ([AI Act Service Desk](https://ai-act-service-desk.ec.europa.eu/en/ai-act/article-111), [artificialintelligenceact.eu](https://artificialintelligenceact.eu/implementation-timeline)).

## Contradictions & Uncertainties
Significant contradictions exist across sources. Several post-Omnibus sources confirm the December 2027 date ([Digital Strategy EC](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai)), while others—apparently not updated—still cite August 2026 as operative ([Responsible AI Labs](https://responsibleailabs.ai/knowledge-hub/articles/eu-ai-act-august-2026-compliance)). The European Parliament's overview states a 36-month (≈August 2027) timeline (medium confidence), inconsistent with both other dates ([European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/topics/en/article/20230601STO93804/eu-ai-act-first-regulation-on-artificial-intelligence)). Several low-confidence claims (below 0.4) should be flagged: the Article 113 consolidated text interpretation (claim_008, 0.12), the "general application" distinction (claim_011, 0.12), unreconciled industry claims about August 2026 (claim_012, 0.17), the "backstop" framing (claim_013, 0.12), and an ambiguous Squire Patton Boggs timeline listing multiple dates without clarification (claim_015, 0.12).

## Knowledge Gaps
Unresolved questions include: whether any Annex III sub-categories retain the original August 2026 date; the exact official citation number for the Omnibus Regulation (informally cited as "2026/1744" but unconfirmed in official sources); whether the Article 111(2) grandfathering rule has been substantively amended beyond the date shift; whether EU guidance pages have been fully updated to reflect the Omnibus; and whether standards-readiness confirmation remains a precondition for the December 2027 date or is now fixed unconditionally.
